purpose: Free, local GGUF models that can drive a coding agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider) through LUKE's own llama-server. Every entry is filtered by three things an agent cannot work without: a chat template with tool calling, a file small enough to load next to its KV cache on the listed machine tier, and an architecture the pinned llama.cpp build already understands.

backend.note: A model released after the pinned build needs a newer backend: LLAMA_RELEASE=b<newer> ./scripts/setup/setup-llama.sh. Every model below predates b9668.

agentNeeds.note: Claude Code's own system prompt and tool schemas are a large slice of the window before a single file is read. Below ~16K the loop truncates; 20K is what LUKE allows by default (LUKE_LLM_MAX_CONTEXT raises the ceiling).

rankingSource: quality is an editorial 0-100 for agent work on this class of machine (tool-call reliability first, then code quality); riskLevel marks quants low enough that tool calls may get mangled. A recommendation sorts fits by riskLevel, then quality.
sizeSource: Published file sizes from the quantizer's own repository (bartowski, Qwen, lmstudio-community, unsloth), checked 2026-11-06. A different quantizer's file will differ by a few hundred MB.
kvSource: KV cache is arithmetic, not a guess: layers x KV heads x head dim x 2 (K and V) x 1 byte (q8_0) per token, or the MLA latent for GLM. llama.cpp prints the real number at start-up as 'KV self size' and LUKE records it per model, which replaces this estimate after the first load.

machineProfiles.label: Mac 18 GB (M3 Pro class)
machineProfiles.note: Metal only lets a device address ~14.3 GB of the 18 GB; that is the budget models share (memory-calibration.cjs).

models.label: Qwen2.5-Coder 14B Instruct — Q4_K_M
models.bestFor: The 18 GB Mac default: real tool-call training, and enough headroom left for a 16–20K window.
models.evidence: Trained with an explicit function-call format; the most widely deployed mid-size model in agent CLIs.
models.risk: Weaker than a 30B on multi-file refactors; keep one file per request.

models.label: GLM-4.7-Flash 30B-A3B — IQ2_M
models.bestFor: An 18 GB Mac that wants 30B-class breadth and MoE speed (only ~3B weights are read per token).
models.evidence: MIT weights, 128K training context, a documented tool-call parser, and thinking mode that can be switched off for agents.
models.risk: About 2.8 bits per weight. It fits, but low-bit quants are where tool calls get mangled — keep it only if `luke-agent-env.sh check` reports tool_use and real edits land.

models.label: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct — Q6_K
models.bestFor: The floor that always loads: fast, leaves ~6 GB for context, good for one-file edits and explaining code.
models.evidence: Same tool-use training as the 14B at half the memory.
models.risk: Loses the thread after two or three dependent edits.

models.label: Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B — Q3_K_L
models.bestFor: A 24 GB machine: the strongest open agentic coder that still offloads fully with room for a 20K window.
models.evidence: Built for agentic coding; its card names Claude Code-style scaffolds. Small KV cache (4 KV heads) is why it fits sooner than its size suggests.
models.risk: Does not fit an 18 GB machine: 14.6 GB of weights against a 14.3 GB working set, before any KV cache.

models.label: Devstral Small 2 24B — Q4_K_M
models.bestFor: A 24–32 GB machine doing multi-file edits: trained with All Hands AI for agent scaffolds, not for chat.
models.evidence: Mistral's card reports SWE-bench Verified 68.0 and names Claude Code, Cline, OpenHands and SWE-Agent as targets.
models.risk: Dense, so it is slower per token than an A3B MoE at the same quality; too large for 18 GB.

models.label: Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B — Q4_K_M
models.bestFor: A 32 GB+ machine: the quality point where local agent work stops feeling like a compromise.
models.evidence: Same agentic training as the Q3 version, at the quant most people run.
models.risk: 18.6 GB will not load on 18–24 GB machines without CPU offload and a much smaller window.
